body.instructions:
@@MANUAL@@

## Model sheet of the place (기준 배경 부품 시트)
Sometimes the app sends a model sheet of this place instead of base backgrounds: Image 2 shows the furniture and fittings of this place, each cut out from a finished background of it and boxed on a grey sheet, and plain swatches of its colors (wall, side wall, floor, baseboard). Image 1 is a rough of this place.
- Image 1 decides the camera, the layout and what is in the picture. The sheet has no room and no camera: the position, size and angle of every object come only from Image 1. A sofa that Image 1 shows from the side or at an angle is drawn from the side or at that angle, never turned to face the camera like on the sheet.
- Find every object of Image 1 on the sheet and describe it with its design, colors and two to four key features there (for example "the wine-red tufted sofa with gold claw feet from image 2"). Describe the walls, the floor and the baseboard with the swatch colors.
- Objects of Image 1 that are not on the sheet are drawn as Image 1 shows them, in the same plain look as the furniture on the sheet.
- Never add an object from the sheet where Image 1 shows none.
- Write the marker [SAME PLACE] right after the layout rule (item 5); the app replaces it with the team's sentence about the sheet. Item 6 is for reference images only: do not write it for the sheet.
- The sheet already shows our style for this place, so the app sends no style examples: style_picks must be [] and item 8 is left out.

content.text:
Aspect ratio: 1.44:1 (the image will be 2256x1568, drawn level; the final picture is 16:9, 2048x1152, see Tilt below).
Time of day: day
Place: auto (decide from the sketch)
Perspective: auto (follow the sketch; there is no camera sentence).
Image 1: rough sketch by our artist (layout source), turned level by the app (see Tilt).
Tilt: the artist drew this shot tilted by 12° (a dutch angle, the left side higher). The app turned Image 1 level for you; it will turn the finished picture back by 12° and crop it to the final frame. So draw the picture level, exactly as Image 1 shows it: the horizon and the floor lines run as they run in Image 1, and vertical lines stay vertical. Do not mention the tilt in the prompt; the app adds a sentence about the white corners around the turned sketch.
Image 2: model sheet (기준 배경 부품 시트) of this same place: its furniture and fittings cut out from a finished background of it (the artist's notes in Korean: 창문 쪽), and swatches of its wall, side wall, floor and baseboard colors. Parts the artist named (Korean): 소파.
Style examples: a model sheet is given, so the app sends no style examples this time; style_picks must be [].
Base style strip: always sent as the last image. In the prompt write {BASE} for its number and {S1}, {S2} for the style examples.
Artist's request (Korean): 왼쪽이 올라간 컷.
Write the order sheet now. Follow the manual exactly: its markers or verbatim sentences, the numbers of Image 1 and the model sheet, the placeholders, and the section "Model sheet of the place (기준 배경 부품 시트)" with its [SAME PLACE] marker.

order.prompt: Generate an image of a living room. 1. Layout: image 1, drawn level. Image 2 is the model sheet of this place: its furniture and fittings have exactly these designs and colors, and the walls, floor and baseboard use exactly its swatch colors. Image 2 has no camera and no layout: follow image 1 for the camera, the layout and the position, size and angle of every object. Image 3 shows the target drawing style: a quick freehand brush drawing, like the distant buildings, the white balcony railings, the windows and the trees in image 3. Flat colors with hard edges, clear and fairly saturated, never greyish or washed out; shapes slightly deformed by hand, lines that are not ruler-straight, rectangles a little uneven, thin things like pipes, railings and window bars drawn as single loose brush strokes, almost like a doodle. It must not look wavy or warped. Flat cel shading, no gradients, no glow, no texture, no black outlines. Time: daytime. The interior is lit with even, neutral light and keeps clear, bright, fairly saturated everyday colors; through the windows and doors you see the outside in flat daylight colors. Avoid: sketch lines, labels or handwriting from image 1, ruler-straight vector lines, perfect geometry, wavy distortion, fisheye distortion, black outlines, photorealism, glossy highlights, gradients, soft airbrush, glow, light falloff, light rays, painterly texture, dull greyish or washed-out colors, the playground objects of image 3, people. Image 1 is the sketch turned level on a larger canvas: its white corners are not part of the layout, so continue the scene there plainly (they are cropped away later). Aspect ratio 1.44:1.
